statement: Marisol takes a bus and then a train to work. The bus is on time with probability $0.85$ and the train is on time with probability $0.90$. Whether the bus is on time is independent of whether the train is on time. What is the probability that at least one of them is late on a given day?

choices.misconception: I found the probability that both are late, 0.15 times 0.10, but the question asks for at least one being late.
I added the chances of each being late, 0.15 and 0.10, but that counts the days when both are late twice.
I found the probability that both are on time, 0.85 times 0.90, and forgot to subtract it from 1.

hints: At least one late is the opposite of a simpler event.
The complement of at least one late is both on time. Find that probability using independence.
Both on time has probability $0.85 \times 0.90 = 0.765$. Subtract from $1$.

solutions.reliable: The opposite of at least one being late is both being on time. By independence, $P(\text{both on time}) = 0.85 \times 0.90 = 0.765$. So $P(\text{at least one late}) = 1 - 0.765 = 0.235$.
solutions.elegant: Add the chances of each being late and subtract the overlap: $0.15 + 0.10 - (0.15)(0.10) = 0.25 - 0.015 = 0.235$.
